note: P4348 (Pro 29:15) — the rod and reproof give wisdom; a child left to himself shames his mother.

dims.v: discipline's fruit — the wisdom the rod and reproof impart
the wisdom that the rod and reproof give — the fruit of loving correction in a child, the opposite of the shame an undisciplined child brings, correction as the making of a wise person
the shame of neglect it is set against (266789)
set against the disgrace a child left to himself brings
chokmah (wisdom) — 'the rod and reproof give WISDOM'; correction, firmly and lovingly given, makes a child wise. Discipline is not cruelty but the imparting of wisdom (cf 13:24; 22:15; 29:17).
disgrace — the shame an undisciplined child brings his mother
the shame brought on a mother by a child left to himself — the disgrace of the undisciplined child, the bitter fruit of neglected correction, against the wisdom discipline would have given
the wisdom of correction it is set against (266786)
set against the wisdom the rod and reproof impart

bosh (be ashamed) — 'but a child left to himself brings SHAME to his mother'; neglected discipline yields a child who disgraces his parent. To withhold correction is to prepare shame (cf 29:15a; 10:1).
